data.one_liner: Generates type‑safe CRUD code for Cloud Firestore documents in Flutter.
data.what_it_does: flutterfire_gen reads Dart classes annotated with @FirestoreDocument and produces query and model helpers for reading, creating, updating, and deleting Firestore documents. It handles default values, server timestamps, and FieldValue operations automatically.
use_when: You need compile‑time, type‑safe Firestore access without writing boilerplate.
You want automatic handling of server timestamps and FieldValue operations.
You prefer a single source of truth for document schema in Dart.
avoid_when: You only need runtime Firestore access and prefer a lightweight wrapper.
Your project targets non‑Flutter platforms only.
strengths: Supports default values and FieldValue annotations
weaknesses: Breaks on major version bumps of analyzer/source_gen
Tied to specific Firestore schema annotations
data.setup_notes: Add flutterfire_gen, flutterfire_gen_annotation, flutterfire_gen_utils to dev_dependencies, run build_runner, include part file in source.

alternatives.name: built_value
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides code‑gen for immutable models and serialization without Firestore‑specific helpers.

alternatives.why_pick_it: Generates immutable data classes and unions; can be combined with custom Firestore wrappers.
